name: kmerseek
kind: counts shared k-mers in a reduced alphabet
compares: Short words of k letters (k-mers) shared between two proteins. First, each amino acid is replaced by a letter from a smaller alphabet, for example H for hydrophobic and P for polar. Two proteins can then match where their residues differ but their pattern of residue types is the same.
reference: An index of the relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), built once per alphabet and k-mer length.
score: region_enrichment: the number of k-mers the region shares with the target divided by the number expected by chance (fold enrichment). Higher ranks first. A region was kept when either test passed: its own score was at least 1.3, or the whole query protein's p-value was at most 0.05.
failure_modes: A feature shorter than k residues contains no complete k-mer, so it cannot be found. The strata above show how Fmax changes with region length.
The task script records a kmerseek search that exits with an error as a search with no hits, so a crash would look like a miss. How often that happened in this run: not measured.
Setting hp_thomas_dill2 k33 was scored, but no trace row holds its search task, so its cost is not measured, and the scoring task for it was not found either.

cost_per_1000_queries.hardware: Stanford Sherlock, SLURM partition hns; searches on CPU only

questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.005 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.297 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.000 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.000 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting `gbmr4_k21_lcFalse`; strata with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.208 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.098 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.050 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.281 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.232 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting `gbmr4_k21_lcFalse`.)
Can you spend about 0.0204 CPU-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured cost against zebrafish; the range over relatives is under "Cost per 1,000 queries" above.
